# AGENTS.md — Workspace-level instructions for AI coding agents

> These rules apply to **all** AI-assisted contributions to `deepspeedai/DeepSpeed`.

## Contribution Policy (Mandatory)

### Duplicate-work checks

Before proposing a PR, run these checks:

```bash
gh issue view <issue_number> --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --comments
gh pr list --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --state open --search "<issue_number> in:body"
gh pr list --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --state open --search "<short area keywords>"
```

- If an open PR already addresses the same fix, do not open another.
- If your approach is materially different, explain the difference in the issue.
- DeepSpeed carries long-lived parallel implementations (ZeRO 1/2 vs 3, fp16 vs bf16 optimizers, per-accelerator op builders). Before fixing a bug in one, check whether the sibling paths share the defect, and state in the PR which ones you checked.

### New features need an accepted proposal first

Per [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md#new-feature-contribution-guidelines), a new feature starts with a proposal issue -- description, motivation, rough design, and planned experiments -- that maintainers accept before implementation begins. Do not open a feature PR with no accepted proposal; open the proposal issue instead.

### No low-value busywork PRs

Do not open one-off PRs for tiny edits (a single typo, an isolated style change, a lone type annotation). Mechanical cleanups are acceptable only when bundled with substantive work in the same area. This is the PR-level form of the rule against cosmetic changes below.

### Accountability

- Pure code-agent PRs are **not allowed**. A human submitter must understand and defend the change end-to-end.
- The submitting human must review every changed line and run the relevant tests.
- `Signed-off-by` is a [DCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developer_Certificate_of_Origin) attestation made by a person, not by an agent. Never sign off on a diff that no human has read.
- PR descriptions for AI-assisted work **must** include:
    - Why this does not duplicate an existing PR or issue.
    - Test commands run and their results, including the hardware they ran on: device model and count, accelerator/driver version, and torch version.
    - Convergence, throughput, and peak-memory results when the change affects numerics, performance, or memory -- see [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md#step-1-proposal-and-discussion) for the evidence bar.
    - Which cells of the compatibility matrix (ZeRO stage, offload, precision, parallelism) were validated, and which were not.
    - A clear statement that AI assistance was used.
- Before opening or reviewing a PR, work through the [`/pr-checklist`](.agents/skills/pr-checklist/SKILL.md) skill: design fit, accelerator portability, backward compatibility, on-device validation, diff hygiene, and PR contents.

### Fail-closed behavior

If the work is duplicate, trivial busywork, or an unproposed new feature, **do not proceed**. Return a short explanation of what is missing.

---

## DeepSpeed Project Rules

### Commit & CI requirements

- When creating commits, use `git commit --signoff`.
- DCO compliance is enforced by the required CI check; do not report commit-signoff findings in code reviews.
- Formatting: yapf (column_limit=119, `.style.yapf`) + flake8 (`.flake8`).
- Always verify changed files pass pre-commit checks before committing: `pre-commit run --files <changed_files>`. Only check modified files, not the entire codebase. Config: `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.
- `check-torchdist` hook: NEVER directly import torch's distributed module. Use `import deepspeed.comm as dist` instead.
- New source files (`.py`, `.c`/`.cpp`/`.cu`/`.h`, and the other extensions matched by the `check-license` hook) require license header:
  ```
  # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
  # DeepSpeed Team
  ```

### Code change discipline

- NEVER make cosmetic/formatting-only changes to existing code. Only add/modify lines that are functionally necessary. Minimizing diff noise is critical for code review.
- Delete dead code decisively — if code is unused at runtime (only referenced in tests), remove it along with its tests.
- Prefer consolidating tests over proliferating test files.
- Blend in: when modifying code, read the surrounding context and match the style of neighboring code (naming, spacing, patterns, idioms).
- Write beginner-friendly code: avoid deeply nested expressions or chained logic. Break complex expressions into clear, named intermediate steps.
- Comments should explain **why**, not **what**. Describe the purpose and reasoning, not the mechanics that the code already shows.
- New features must include corresponding tests and documentation updates.
- All changes must not cause `import deepspeed` to initialize CUDA; Keep heavy imports (> 0.1s) out of `import deepspeed`; Avoid changing `deepspeed/__init__.py` unless necessary.

### Test discipline

- Tests verify contracts, not implementations: a test is well-formed only if a different correct implementation of the same contract passes it.
- Before writing a test, name the concrete incorrect behavior it would catch; if you cannot name one, do not write it.
- Assert on observable outcomes through public/stable interfaces; do not assert private method return values or exact internal strings unless pinning a specific fixed bug (justify in a comment).
- Anchor to an external oracle or an independently derived reference instead of re-implementing the logic under test.
- Mocks must stand in for a collaborator's documented contract (schema, protocol), never for internals of the module under test.
- Changes that affect the external contract at the training-loop or inference level require integration tests, not just unit tests (e.g. a minimal training loop with `SimpleModel`).
- Integration tests must be executed on actual devices, not merely written: report the execution hardware spec and results in the PR.

## Tool Caveats

### Edit tool auto-formatter

The Edit tool has a hidden auto-formatter that silently changes quotes, whitespace, blank lines, and line wrapping. For format-sensitive modifications (e.g., when exact formatting matters for pre-commit), use `bash` with `sed`, `python`, or `cat` instead.

It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.

- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

# AGENTS.md — Workspace-level instructions for AI coding agents

> These rules apply to **all** AI-assisted contributions to `deepspeedai/DeepSpeed`.

## Contribution Policy (Mandatory)

### Duplicate-work checks

Before proposing a PR, run these checks:

```bash
gh issue view <issue_number> --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --comments
gh pr list --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --state open --search "<issue_number> in:body"
gh pr list --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --state open --search "<short area keywords>"
```

- If an open PR already addresses the same fix, do not open another.
- If your approach is materially different, explain the difference in the issue.
- DeepSpeed carries long-lived parallel implementations (ZeRO 1/2 vs 3, fp16 vs bf16 optimizers, per-accelerator op builders). Before fixing a bug in one, check whether the sibling paths share the defect, and state in the PR which ones you checked.

### New features need an accepted proposal first

Per [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md#new-feature-contribution-guidelines), a new feature starts with a proposal issue -- description, motivation, rough design, and planned experiments -- that maintainers accept before implementation begins. Do not open a feature PR with no accepted proposal; open the proposal issue instead.

### No low-value busywork PRs

Do not open one-off PRs for tiny edits (a single typo, an isolated style change, a lone type annotation). Mechanical cleanups are acceptable only when bundled with substantive work in the same area. This is the PR-level form of the rule against cosmetic changes below.

### Accountability

- Pure code-agent PRs are **not allowed**. A human submitter must understand and defend the change end-to-end.
- The submitting human must review every changed line and run the relevant tests.
- `Signed-off-by` is a [DCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developer_Certificate_of_Origin) attestation made by a person, not by an agent. Never sign off on a diff that no human has read.
- PR descriptions for AI-assisted work **must** include:
    - Why this does not duplicate an existing PR or issue.
    - Test commands run and their results, including the hardware they ran on: device model and count, accelerator/driver version, and torch version.
    - Convergence, throughput, and peak-memory results when the change affects numerics, performance, or memory -- see [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md#step-1-proposal-and-discussion) for the evidence bar.
    - Which cells of the compatibility matrix (ZeRO stage, offload, precision, parallelism) were validated, and which were not.
    - A clear statement that AI assistance was used.
- Before opening or reviewing a PR, work through the [`/pr-checklist`](.agents/skills/pr-checklist/SKILL.md) skill: design fit, accelerator portability, backward compatibility, on-device validation, diff hygiene, and PR contents.

### Fail-closed behavior

If the work is duplicate, trivial busywork, or an unproposed new feature, **do not proceed**. Return a short explanation of what is missing.

---

## DeepSpeed Project Rules

### Commit & CI requirements

- When creating commits, use `git commit --signoff`.
- DCO compliance is enforced by the required CI check; do not report commit-signoff findings in code reviews.
- Formatting: yapf (column_limit=119, `.style.yapf`) + flake8 (`.flake8`).
- Always verify changed files pass pre-commit checks before committing: `pre-commit run --files <changed_files>`. Only check modified files, not the entire codebase. Config: `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.
- `check-torchdist` hook: NEVER directly import torch's distributed module. Use `import deepspeed.comm as dist` instead.
- New source files (`.py`, `.c`/`.cpp`/`.cu`/`.h`, and the other extensions matched by the `check-license` hook) require license header:
  ```
  # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
  # DeepSpeed Team
  ```

### Code change discipline

- NEVER make cosmetic/formatting-only changes to existing code. Only add/modify lines that are functionally necessary. Minimizing diff noise is critical for code review.
- Delete dead code decisively — if code is unused at runtime (only referenced in tests), remove it along with its tests.
- Prefer consolidating tests over proliferating test files.
- Blend in: when modifying code, read the surrounding context and match the style of neighboring code (naming, spacing, patterns, idioms).
- Write beginner-friendly code: avoid deeply nested expressions or chained logic. Break complex expressions into clear, named intermediate steps.
- Comments should explain **why**, not **what**. Describe the purpose and reasoning, not the mechanics that the code already shows.
- New features must include corresponding tests and documentation updates.
- All changes must not cause `import deepspeed` to initialize CUDA; Keep heavy imports (> 0.1s) out of `import deepspeed`; Avoid changing `deepspeed/__init__.py` unless necessary.

### Test discipline

- Tests verify contracts, not implementations: a test is well-formed only if a different correct implementation of the same contract passes it.
- Before writing a test, name the concrete incorrect behavior it would catch; if you cannot name one, do not write it.
- Assert on observable outcomes through public/stable interfaces; do not assert private method return values or exact internal strings unless pinning a specific fixed bug (justify in a comment).
- Anchor to an external oracle or an independently derived reference instead of re-implementing the logic under test.
- Mocks must stand in for a collaborator's documented contract (schema, protocol), never for internals of the module under test.
- Changes that affect the external contract at the training-loop or inference level require integration tests, not just unit tests (e.g. a minimal training loop with `SimpleModel`).
- Integration tests must be executed on actual devices, not merely written: report the execution hardware spec and results in the PR.

13	## 2. 前置知识
14	
15	### 2.1 Python 对象生命周期与垃圾回收
16	
17	- **引用计数**：Python 中每个对象记录「谁在引用我」。引用数归零，对象立即释放。只要还有一个引用活着（哪怕是一个已经「不用了」的 hook），对象及其持有的所有显存/内存就不会释放。
18	- **循环垃圾回收（gc）**：引用计数处理不了循环引用（A 引用 B、B 引用 A），由 `gc` 模块周期性回收。`gc.collect()` 可以强制立刻回收。
19	- **`weakref.ref(obj)`**：弱引用不增加引用计数。`ref()` 返回 `None` 就说明对象已被回收——这是验证「对象真的被释放了」的标准手法。
20	- **`__del__` 析构函数**：对象被回收前调用。它可能在解释器退出的任意时刻、甚至在新对象已经接管了旧资源之后才执行，所以析构逻辑必须容忍「我引用的世界已经变了」。
21	
22	### 2.2 PyTorch 的 hook 机制
23	
24	`module.register_forward_pre_hook(fn)` 会返回一个 `RemovableHandle`，调用它的 `remove()` 才能摘除 hook。关键陷阱：hook 函数通常是**闭包**——它捕获了定义它时的外部变量。如果闭包里捕获了引擎（`self`），那么只要 hook 还挂在模型上，**模型就把引擎（连同引擎持有的优化器、fp32 主权重、梯度缓冲）钉在内存里**。HF Trainer 的使用模式正是「反复销毁引擎但保留模型」，于是每次都泄漏一整个引擎的状态。
25

27	
28	DeepSpeed 不会直接用你传入的优化器做 step。你的 `torch.optim.Adam` 是「最里层」；外面按配置包上 ZeRO 优化器（梯度切分/通信）或 fp16/bf16 优化器（主权重管理/loss scaling）。理解这条包装链，才能看懂 `engine.optimizer.step()` 到底执行了什么。

143	**练习 1**：为什么 `del autoep_replacement_sources`（[engine.py:600-602](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/b9100c541ac1b8e25148bc8000d1ad45c4c095db/deepspeed/runtime/engine.py#L600-L602)）不能省？

149	**答案**：MPI 启动（`mpirun`）不设置 `LOCAL_RANK`，而是设置 `OMPI_COMM_WORLD_LOCAL_RANK`。引擎要求 `LOCAL_RANK` 存在（`_do_args_sanity_check` 断言），所以这里把 MPI 变量对齐到 `LOCAL_RANK`，并在两者同时存在时断言一致，防止启动器信息冲突。
150	
151	**练习 3**：把 `_configure_distributed_model` 挪到 `_configure_expert_parallel` 之前会发生什么？
152	
153	**答案**：`_configure_distributed_model` 会在当前（未注入的）模型上做混合精度 cast 与设备迁移，并探测 MoE 层写入 `self.has_moe_layers`。AutoEP 注入发生在其后的话，cast/迁移作用在即将被丢弃的旧模块上，且 `has_moe_layers` 探测不到新注入的专家层，后续优化器分组、专家并行组都会出错。这个顺序是「先换模块、再配置模型、最后包优化器」的固定链条。

155	### 4.2 确定性策略的应用点：apply_determinism
156	
157	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
158	
159	`deterministic_mode`（u8-l8 会系统讲）是一个 opt-in 的确定性执行开关。它的难点在于**时机**：cuBLAS 的工作区配置（`CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG`）必须在 CUDA 初始化之前由环境变量决定，`torch.use_deterministic_algorithms` 也应在任何算子执行前打开。一旦某个阶段跑过非确定性内核，再开开关也无法回头。因此引擎把应用点放在 `__init__` 的**第一批属性初始化之后、一切模型/优化器/通信配置之前**。

216

296	### 4.4 并行组初始化与模块注入的调用点
297	
298	#### 4.4.1 概念说明
299	
300	阶段 3 的两个注入器（AutoEP、AutoTP）都会**替换用户模型里的模块**，从而改变参数对象与进程组需求。这带来两个必须在引擎构造期解决的问题：
301	
302	1. **参数重映射**：用户若把 `model.parameters()` 提前物化成列表传给 `initialize()`，注入替换参数后列表里全是失效对象，必须按 `replacement_sources` 重映射。
303	2. **冻结参数记录**：AutoTP 切分后，一部分参数在各 rank 间是复制（replicated）的。可训练的复制参数需要梯度 all-reduce hook；**冻结**（`requires_grad=False`）的则跳过——但引擎要记下清单（`_autotp_frozen_replicated_params`），因为用户之后若解冻它们，梯度不会走复制路径，训练会静默漂移，所以引擎选择在 backward 前直接报错（u6-l1 详讲）。
304	
305	进程组方面：AutoEP 会创建专家并行（EP）与专家数据并行（EDP）组，AutoTP 会初始化 TP mesh——它们都发生在优化器包装**之前**，因为 ZeRO 构造时就要拿这些组来划分分区。
306

311	  ├─ _model_parameters_need_remap?            # 用户显式传了参数列表？

313	  │     validate_autoep_config → build_folding_spec → validate_folding_global
314	  │     groups._create_expert_and_data_parallel(...)   # 建 EP/EDP 进程组
315	  │     替换 MoE 层，返回 replacement_sources
316	  ├─ 重映射 client optimizer 的 param_groups / 用户的参数列表
317	  ├─ autotp_size() > 1:
318	  │     _configure_tensor_parallel(model, tp_config)
319	  │       ├─ _configure_tensor_parallel_states: 初始化 TP mesh、注册 first_dataloader_check hook
320	  │       └─ _apply_autotp_partitioning: AutoTP 切分、finalize_autotp 里
321	  │            self._autotp_frozen_replicated_params = autotp.register_replicated_grad_hooks(model)
322	  └─ resolve_per_head_muon_after_sharding(model)   # Muon 按头数配置折算到切分后的参数

362	### 4.5 destroy()/__del__ 生命周期与引用清理（本周期 #9034）
363	
364	#### 4.5.1 概念说明
365	
366	HF Trainer 等上层框架的使用模式是：**反复对同一个模型 build → train → destroy → build → train → ...**（例如每个 epoch 重建引擎）。修复前（issue #7204）这会泄漏 GiB 级显存与主机内存，根因是一张「模型 → 引擎 → 优化器」的隐性引用网：
367	
368	1. **模型挂着的 hooks 引用引擎**：`module_forward_pre_hook`/`module_forward_post_hook`（以及 AutoTP 路径的 `first_dataloader_check`）都是闭包，捕获 `self`（引擎）。模型活着 → hook 活着 → 引擎活着 → 优化器、fp32 主权重、扁平梯度缓冲全部活着。
369	2. **参数属性反向引用优化器**：ZeRO-3 给参数留 `p._z3_optimizer`；ZeRO-1/2 卸载留 `lp._zero_optimizer`；BF16 优化器的 `_update_hp_grad` 给每个 bf16 参数留 `lp._hp_grad`——指向整块扁平 fp32 梯度缓冲的**视图**（约 2 倍 bf16 模型大小），视图会让整个 storage 活着。
370	3. **进程级栈泄漏**：ZeRO-3 的 `setup_zero_stage3_hooks` 把顶层模块压入进程级 `FWD_MODULE_STACK`，从不弹出——每个销毁的模型（及其引擎）永久存活。
371	4. **类级缓存的隐性钉住**：参数协调器的 `__params_to_release` 原是**类级** `functools.lru_cache`，以 `self` 为 key、永不失效——所有协调器及其引用的模块、参数被钉住到进程结束。
372	5. **`__del__` 的二次拆除**：显式 `destroy()` 后，对象最终被 GC 回收时 `__del__` 会**再次**执行 `destroy()`。此时同一个模型可能已被**新引擎**包装：二次拆除会清掉属于新引擎的状态（典型如 `_hp_mapping`），把新引擎弄坏。
373	
374	#9034 的修复思路：`destroy()` 幂等化（`_destroyed` 标记）+ 把上面每一条引用逐一斩断。
375	
376	#### 4.5.2 核心流程
377	
378	销毁链的执行顺序（顺序有意为之）：
379	
380	```text
381	engine.destroy()                          # 用户显式调用
382	  └─ self._destroyed = True               # 先立标记（幂等 + __del__ 跳过依据）
383	  └─ destroy_exchanges(module)            # 只释放本引擎的 DeepEP 缓冲
384	  └─ 释放 DeepCompile 编译态 / dynamo 配置
385	  └─ optimizer.destroy()                  # 各优化器清理反向引用：
386	  │     ZeRO-3 (stage3):      parameter_offload.destroy()  → 摘模块 hook + 弹 FWD_MODULE_STACK（至多一次）
387	  │                            p._z3_optimizer = None、unpin 卸载缓冲
388	  │     ZeRO-1/2 (stage_1_and_2): p._hp_mapping = None、del p._zero_optimizer、unpin
389	  │     BF16:                  lp._hp_mapping = None、lp._hp_grad = None、摘 grad acc hooks
390	  └─ _deactivate_deepcompile()            # 若 DeepCompile 激活：先走它（会重新挂 forward hooks）
391	  └─ 摘除并置空三个引擎 hook:              # 必须在 _deactivate_deepcompile 之后！
392	        module_forward_pre_hook / module_forward_post_hook / first_dataloader_check
393	  └─ debug_clear_module_and_param_names()
394	  └─ decoupled checkpoint engine cleanup
395	  finally: 释放 python_gc 手持的代际
396	
397	engine.__del__()                          # GC 兜底
398	  └─ if self._destroyed: return           # 已显式销毁 → 直接返回，防止二次拆除
399	  └─ 否则 try destroy()（异常仅 debug 日志）
400	```

454	**答案**：类级 `functools.lru_cache` 装饰方法时，缓存的 key 包含 `self`，且缓存永不失效——每个调用过的实例都永久留在缓存里，实例又引用模块与参数。改成每实例（`__init__` 里对绑定方法再包一层 `lru_cache`）后，缓存生命周期与实例绑定：实例可回收，缓存随之消失，缓存效果（按 `(submodule, step_id)` 记忆待释放参数集）不变。
455	
456	**练习 4**：`destroy()` 里清反向引用时为什么用 `getattr(p, '_z3_optimizer', None) is self` 而不是无脑置空？
457	
458	**答案**：模型可能已被新引擎包装，新优化器可能已经把自己的引用写进同一属性。身份判断 `is self` 确保只清除「确实指向自己」的引用，不误伤后来者的状态——这正是二次拆除问题在优化器层面的对应防线。
459	
460	## 5. 综合实践
461	
462	**任务：为「引擎生命周期」写一份带证据的实验报告**
463	
464	把本讲的两条主线串起来：构造期顺序 + 销毁期清理。建议流程：
465	
466	1. **准备**：基于 `tests/unit/simple_model.py` 的 `SimpleModel` 写一个可配置的训练脚本（config 用字典传入），支持 `zero_stage`、`offload`、`bf16` 三个开关。
467	2. **构造期**：开 `torch` 日志或直接观察 stdout，收集 `DeepSpeed Basic Optimizer` 与 `DeepSpeed Final Optimizer` 两行日志，对 ZeRO-1/2/3、bf16 四种配置各记录一次 (basic, final) 类型对，对照 4.3.2 的分发图打勾。
468	3. **销毁期**：在脚本里实现「build → train 4 步 → destroy → build → train 4 步 → destroy」的循环，每轮结束后：
469	   - `gc.collect()`；
470	   - 用 `weakref` 断言上一轮引擎与优化器已被回收（仿 [test_zero.py:2332-2343](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/b9100c541ac1b8e25148bc8000d1ad45c4c095db/tests/unit/v1/zero/test_zero.py#L2332-L2343)）；
471	   - 若在 GPU 上：记录 `torch.cuda.memory_allocated()`，观察多轮循环后是否线性增长（增长即泄漏）。
472	4. **输出**：一页报告，含 (a) 八阶段清单及行号（4.1.4 的成果）、(b) 优化器包装类型表、(c) 各轮显存曲线与 weakref 断言结果。
473	5. 全部结果依赖本地环境，**待本地验证**；若暂无 GPU，步骤 3 的显存观察可换成 `tracemalloc` 统计主机内存，销毁断言部分在 CPU 后端同样可跑（ZeRO 1/2 不依赖 GPU）。
474	
475	## 6. 本讲小结
476	
477	- `DeepSpeedEngine.__init__` 有清晰八阶段骨架：基础属性+确定性 → 校验 → AutoEP/AutoTP 注入 → 分布式环境 → 模型配置+hooks → 数据加载 → 优化器包装 → 检查点与收尾；后续所有子系统都在这张地图上有明确插入点。
478	- 优化器是三层结构：client optimizer → `basic_optimizer`（真实更新者）→ `engine.optimizer`（ZeRO/fp16/bf16 包装器）；两行日志即可验证。
479	- `deterministic_mode` 在 `__init__` 最早期经 `apply_determinism` 生效：仅支持 NVIDIA CUDA、要求预先设置 `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG`，检查前置是因为 cuBLAS 工作区在 CUDA 初始化后无法更改。
480	- AutoEP/AutoTP 注入会替换模块与参数，因此必须先于优化器包装，并带出参数重映射、`_autotp_frozen_replicated_params` 冻结清单、`first_dataloader_check` 一次性 hook 等配套机制。
481	- 本周期 #9034 补全了销毁链：`destroy()` 先立 `_destroyed` 标记、摘除三个闭包引用引擎的 hooks（在 `_deactivate_deepcompile` 之后）、各优化器清理 `p._z3_optimizer`/`lp._zero_optimizer`/`lp._hp_grad` 反向引用、弹 `FWD_MODULE_STACK`、协调器缓存改为每实例；`__del__` 检查 `_destroyed` 防止 GC 期二次拆除破坏新引擎。
482	- `TestDestroyReleasesEngine` 用 weakref + storage 指针 + gc 的组合，把「销毁后可回收」固化为七场景回归契约。
483	
484	## 7. 下一步学习建议
485	
486	- **u2-l4（训练主循环）**：本讲注册的 `module_forward_pre_hook` 触发的 `_forward_prologue`、梯度累积边界判定、`register_grad_acc_post_hook` 支持的 PyTorch 风格 backward，都将在 `train_batch`/`backward`/`step` 的时序中展开。

# u2-l3 引擎构造与销毁：DeepSpeedEngine 生命周期全流程

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 按顺序列出 `DeepSpeedEngine.__init__` 的 8 个关键阶段，并为每个阶段指出对应的源码方法与行号。
2. 理解三层优化器关系：用户传入的 `optimizer`（client optimizer）、`basic_optimizer`、`engine.optimizer` 分别是什么、在哪一步被包装。
3. 说明 `deterministic_mode` 为何必须在引擎构造的最早期应用，以及 `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG` 前置检查的必要性。
4. 弄清 AutoEP/AutoTP 模块注入、`_autotp_frozen_replicated_params` 冻结参数记录、`first_dataloader_check` 等「改变模型或挂 hook」的动作发生在初始化的哪一步。
5. 追踪本周期（提交 `f32e164b9`，PR #9034，修复 issue #7204）补全的销毁链：`destroy()` 如何摘除闭包引用引擎的 forward hooks、`__del__` 如何用 `_destroyed` 标记防止二次拆除、各优化器如何清理指回自己的参数属性（`p._z3_optimizer`、`lp._zero_optimizer`、`lp._hp_grad`、`FWD_MODULE_STACK` 弹栈、协调器的每实例 `lru_cache`）。

## 2. 前置知识

### 2.1 Python 对象生命周期与垃圾回收

- **引用计数**：Python 中每个对象记录「谁在引用我」。引用数归零，对象立即释放。只要还有一个引用活着（哪怕是一个已经「不用了」的 hook），对象及其持有的所有显存/内存就不会释放。
- **循环垃圾回收（gc）**：引用计数处理不了循环引用（A 引用 B、B 引用 A），由 `gc` 模块周期性回收。`gc.collect()` 可以强制立刻回收。
- **`weakref.ref(obj)`**：弱引用不增加引用计数。`ref()` 返回 `None` 就说明对象已被回收——这是验证「对象真的被释放了」的标准手法。
- **`__del__` 析构函数**：对象被回收前调用。它可能在解释器退出的任意时刻、甚至在新对象已经接管了旧资源之后才执行，所以析构逻辑必须容忍「我引用的世界已经变了」。

### 2.2 PyTorch 的 hook 机制

`module.register_forward_pre_hook(fn)` 会返回一个 `RemovableHandle`，调用它的 `remove()` 才能摘除 hook。关键陷阱：hook 函数通常是**闭包**——它捕获了定义它时的外部变量。如果闭包里捕获了引擎（`self`），那么只要 hook 还挂在模型上，**模型就把引擎（连同引擎持有的优化器、fp32 主权重、梯度缓冲）钉在内存里**。HF Trainer 的使用模式正是「反复销毁引擎但保留模型」，于是每次都泄漏一整个引擎的状态。

### 2.3 包装器模式

DeepSpeed 不会直接用你传入的优化器做 step。你的 `torch.optim.Adam` 是「最里层」；外面按配置包上 ZeRO 优化器（梯度切分/通信）或 fp16/bf16 优化器（主权重管理/loss scaling）。理解这条包装链，才能看懂 `engine.optimizer.step()` 到底执行了什么。

### 2.4 与上一讲的衔接

上一讲（u2-l2）我们看到 `DeepSpeedConfig` 在**配置层**解析 `deterministic_mode`（`configure_determinism` 只是把布尔值写到 `config.deterministic_mode` 上）。本讲看**引擎层**：`DeepSpeedEngine.__init__` 在拿到 config 后的第一时间调用 `apply_determinism` 真正生效。这种「解析在 config、应用在 engine」的两阶段设计是 DeepSpeed 的常见模式。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 引擎构造主线：八个阶段

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

`deepspeed.initialize()` 把模型、优化器、配置交给我们之后，真正干活的是 `DeepSpeedEngine.__init__`。这个构造函数长达约 270 行（[engine.py:518-786](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/b9100c541ac1b8e25148bc8000d1ad45c4c095db/deepspeed/runtime/engine.py#L518-L786)），但它有清晰的骨架。把骨架拆出来，就得到了后续所有讲义（ZeRO、AutoTP、混合精度）在初始化中的「插入点」地图。

为什么要强调顺序？因为这个函数里很多步骤**互相依赖**：AutoEP 必须在优化器之前替换模块（否则优化器持有的是被丢弃的旧专家权重）；确定性策略必须在任何 CUDA 算子跑起来之前应用；forward hooks 必须在优化器包装之后注册（否则 DeepCompile 无法改造它们）。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

`__init__` 的八个阶段（按代码执行顺序）：

```text
阶段 1  基础属性 + 确定性策略
        保存 config，若 deterministic_mode=True 则 apply_determinism()
阶段 2  参数与配置校验
        _do_args_sanity_check → _configure_with_arguments → _do_sanity_check
阶段 3  AutoEP / AutoTP 模块注入
        _configure_expert_parallel → （autotp_size>1 时）_configure_tensor_parallel
        含 _autotp_frozen_replicated_params 冻结参数记录、first_dataloader_check hook
阶段 4  分布式环境与监控
        _set_distributed_vars（绑定设备、rank）→ dist.configure → MonitorMaster
阶段 5  分布式模型配置与引擎 hooks
        _configure_distributed_model（混合精度 cast、设备迁移、MoE 探测）
        注册 module_forward_pre_hook / module_forward_post_hook
阶段 6  数据加载器与计时器
        training_data → deepspeed_io；SynchronizedWallClockTimer 等
阶段 7  优化器与调度器包装（三层包装链的核心）
        _configure_optimizer → basic_optimizer → engine.optimizer
        _configure_lr_scheduler
阶段 8  检查点引擎与收尾
        _configure_checkpointing（决定谁写检查点）
        engine_timers、compile pass 注册、torch 风格 backward 支持判定
```

注意：**检查点加载**（`load_checkpoint`）不发生在 `__init__` 里——它是用户在 `initialize()` 之后显式调用的公共方法；`__init__` 里只完成阶段 8 的「检查点引擎配置」（决定哪个 rank 写、写到哪里）。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

构造函数签名与最初的属性初始化——引擎是 `torch.nn.Module` 的子类，把用户的模型挂在自己的 `module` 属性下：

- [engine.py:518-550](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/b9100c541ac1b8e25148bc8000d1ad45c4c095db/deepspeed/runtime/engine.py#L518-L550) — `__init__` 接收 `args/model/optimizer/model_parameters/config...`，先把步数计数器、MoE 容器、优化器占位（`self.optimizer = None`、`self.basic_optimizer = None`）等基础属性铺好，并保存 `config`（原始 JSON 侧）与 `config_class`（解析后的 `DeepSpeedConfig`）。

阶段 1 的确定性策略应用点（详见 4.2）：

- [engine.py:551-553](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/b9100c541ac1b8e25148bc8000d1ad45c4c095db/deepspeed/runtime/engine.py#L551-L553) — 只要 `deterministic_mode` 为真，立刻导入并调用 `apply_determinism(self._config)`。此时任何模型参数还没被 cast、任何 CUDA 上下文（通常）还没建立。

阶段 4 的分布式环境：

- [engine.py:614-618](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/b9100c541ac1b8e25148bc8000d1ad45c4c095db/deepspeed/runtime/engine.py#L614-L618) — `_set_distributed_vars(args)`（[engine.py:1973-1983](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/b9100c541ac1b8e25148bc8000d1ad45c4c095db/deepspeed/runtime/engine.py#L1973-L1983)：`device_rank >= 0` 时 `get_accelerator().set_device()` 绑定本卡、从 `dist` 取 `world_size/global_rank`；否则退化为单进程 `world_size=1`）；`dist.configure(self._config)` 配通信层；`MonitorMaster` 建监控。

- [engine.py:636](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/b9100c541ac1b8e25148bc8000d1ad45c4c095db/deepspeed/runtime/engine.py#L636) — `self.param_names = {param: name ...}`：参数对象到名字的反查表，后续 `zero_to_fp32` 权重导出要用。

阶段 6 的数据加载器：

### 4.2 确定性策略的应用点：apply_determinism

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

`deterministic_mode`（u8-l8 会系统讲）是一个 opt-in 的确定性执行开关。它的难点在于**时机**：cuBLAS 的工作区配置（`CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG`）必须在 CUDA 初始化之前由环境变量决定，`torch.use_deterministic_algorithms` 也应在任何算子执行前打开。一旦某个阶段跑过非确定性内核，再开开关也无法回头。因此引擎把应用点放在 `__init__` 的**第一批属性初始化之后、一切模型/优化器/通信配置之前**。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

```text
JSON: "deterministic_mode": true
  └─> DeepSpeedConfig 构造期: configure_determinism() 解析布尔值（u2-l2 已讲）
        └─> DeepSpeedEngine.__init__ 早期: apply_determinism(config)
              ├─ config.deterministic_mode 为 False → 直接返回
              ├─ 非 NVIDIA CUDA 后端（KLXPU/ROCm/CPU…）→ ValueError
              ├─ CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG 不是 :4096:8 或 :16:8 → ValueError
              └─ 全部通过:
                    torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)
                    关闭 TF32（matmul 与 cudnn）、关 cudnn.benchmark、开 cudnn.deterministic
```

### 4.3 优化器三层包装链

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

引擎里同时存在三个「优化器」名字，初学者极易混淆：

| 名字 | 是什么 | 谁创建 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `optimizer`（`initialize()` 参数，即 client optimizer） | 用户传入的 `torch.optim.*` 实例、可调用对象，或 `None`（用 JSON 配置声明） | 用户 |
| `self.basic_optimizer` | 最里层的真实优化器：要么就是用户的优化器，要么由 JSON 的 `optimizer.type` 从零构建（如 `DeepSpeedCPUAdam`、`FusedAdam`） | `_configure_optimizer` |
| `self.optimizer` | 引擎对外暴露的最终优化器：在 basic 之外包上 ZeRO/fp16/bf16 包装器，实现梯度切分、主权重管理、loss scaling | `_configure_optimizer` 按配置分发 |

`engine.step()` 调用的是 `self.optimizer`；`self.optimizer` 内部在合适的时机调用 `self.basic_optimizer`（或其 param_groups）做真正的参数更新。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

```text
_configure_optimizer(client_optimizer, model_parameters)
  ├─ client_optimizer is None:
  │     MoE 模型先 configure_moe_param_groups 分组
  │     basic = _configure_basic_optimizer(model_parameters)   # 从 JSON 构建最优实现
  ├─ client_optimizer 是实例/可调用:
  │     basic = client_optimizer（实例）或 client_optimizer(params)（可调用）
  │     ZeRO CPU 卸载 + 非 DeepSpeedCPUAdam/CPULion → 默认直接报错（zero_force_ds_cpu_optimizer）
  ├─ 过滤空 param_groups、查重
  ├─ self.basic_optimizer = basic
  ├─ wrapper = _do_optimizer_sanity_check(basic)   # 决定包装方向
  └─ 按 wrapper 分发:
        ZERO_OPTIMIZATION → _configure_zero_optimizer(basic)   # ZeRO-1/2/3
        FP16 / DDP_BFLOAT16 → _configure_fp16_optimizer(basic, lp_dtype)
        BFLOAT16           → _configure_bf16_optimizer(basic)
        其他               → self.optimizer = basic（裸用）
```

### 4.4 并行组初始化与模块注入的调用点

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

阶段 3 的两个注入器（AutoEP、AutoTP）都会**替换用户模型里的模块**，从而改变参数对象与进程组需求。这带来两个必须在引擎构造期解决的问题：

1. **参数重映射**：用户若把 `model.parameters()` 提前物化成列表传给 `initialize()`，注入替换参数后列表里全是失效对象，必须按 `replacement_sources` 重映射。
2. **冻结参数记录**：AutoTP 切分后，一部分参数在各 rank 间是复制（replicated）的。可训练的复制参数需要梯度 all-reduce hook；**冻结**（`requires_grad=False`）的则跳过——但引擎要记下清单（`_autotp_frozen_replicated_params`），因为用户之后若解冻它们，梯度不会走复制路径，训练会静默漂移，所以引擎选择在 backward 前直接报错（u6-l1 详讲）。

进程组方面：AutoEP 会创建专家并行（EP）与专家数据并行（EDP）组，AutoTP 会初始化 TP mesh——它们都发生在优化器包装**之前**，因为 ZeRO 构造时就要拿这些组来划分分区。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

```text
__init__ 阶段 3
  ├─ _model_parameters_need_remap?            # 用户显式传了参数列表？
  ├─ _configure_expert_parallel(model)        # AutoEP：
  │     validate_autoep_config → build_folding_spec → validate_folding_global
  │     groups._create_expert_and_data_parallel(...)   # 建 EP/EDP 进程组
  │     替换 MoE 层，返回 replacement_sources
  ├─ 重映射 client optimizer 的 param_groups / 用户的参数列表
  ├─ autotp_size() > 1:
  │     _configure_tensor_parallel(model, tp_config)
  │       ├─ _configure_tensor_parallel_states: 初始化 TP mesh、注册 first_dataloader_check hook
  │       └─ _apply_autotp_partitioning: AutoTP 切分、finalize_autotp 里
  │            self._autotp_frozen_replicated_params = autotp.register_replicated_grad_hooks(model)
  └─ resolve_per_head_muon_after_sharding(model)   # Muon 按头数配置折算到切分后的参数
```

#### 4.4.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：AutoEP 注入为什么必须在优化器包装之前？给出两条理由。

**答案**：(1) 优化器的 param_groups 持有参数对象引用，注入替换参数后旧引用全部失效（所以需要 `replacement_sources` 重映射）；(2) ZeRO 优化器构造时要按进程组划分参数分区，EP/EDP 组必须先建好。

**练习 2**：`_autotp_frozen_replicated_params` 记录的是什么？为什么引擎要拒绝「事后解冻」？

**答案**：记录 AutoTP 切分后因 `requires_grad=False` 而被 `register_replicated_grad_hooks` 跳过梯度同步的复制参数。事后解冻它们，梯度不会走复制参数的 all-reduce 路径（hook 注册时就被跳过了），各 rank 梯度不再一致，训练静默漂移；引擎在 backward 前检查并在发现时抛错，宁可显式失败也不静默出错。

**练习 3**：`first_dataloader_check` 与 `module_forward_pre_hook` 都是 forward pre-hook，有何区别？

**答案**：`first_dataloader_check` 是 AutoTP 路径注册的**一次性**检查 hook（`prepend=True`，通过后自摘除），职责是保证 TP 组各 rank 收到相同输入；`module_forward_pre_hook` 是引擎级**常驻** hook（`_create_module_forward_pre_hook` 工厂创建，触发 `_forward_prologue` 做内存统计、profiler 启动等每步工作）。两者都会被 `destroy()` 摘除。

### 4.5 destroy()/__del__ 生命周期与引用清理（本周期 #9034）

#### 4.5.1 概念说明

HF Trainer 等上层框架的使用模式是：**反复对同一个模型 build → train → destroy → build → train → ...**（例如每个 epoch 重建引擎）。修复前（issue #7204）这会泄漏 GiB 级显存与主机内存，根因是一张「模型 → 引擎 → 优化器」的隐性引用网：

1. **模型挂着的 hooks 引用引擎**：`module_forward_pre_hook`/`module_forward_post_hook`（以及 AutoTP 路径的 `first_dataloader_check`）都是闭包，捕获 `self`（引擎）。模型活着 → hook 活着 → 引擎活着 → 优化器、fp32 主权重、扁平梯度缓冲全部活着。
2. **参数属性反向引用优化器**：ZeRO-3 给参数留 `p._z3_optimizer`；ZeRO-1/2 卸载留 `lp._zero_optimizer`；BF16 优化器的 `_update_hp_grad` 给每个 bf16 参数留 `lp._hp_grad`——指向整块扁平 fp32 梯度缓冲的**视图**（约 2 倍 bf16 模型大小），视图会让整个 storage 活着。
3. **进程级栈泄漏**：ZeRO-3 的 `setup_zero_stage3_hooks` 把顶层模块压入进程级 `FWD_MODULE_STACK`，从不弹出——每个销毁的模型（及其引擎）永久存活。
4. **类级缓存的隐性钉住**：参数协调器的 `__params_to_release` 原是**类级** `functools.lru_cache`，以 `self` 为 key、永不失效——所有协调器及其引用的模块、参数被钉住到进程结束。
5. **`__del__` 的二次拆除**：显式 `destroy()` 后，对象最终被 GC 回收时 `__del__` 会**再次**执行 `destroy()`。此时同一个模型可能已被**新引擎**包装：二次拆除会清掉属于新引擎的状态（典型如 `_hp_mapping`），把新引擎弄坏。

#9034 的修复思路：`destroy()` 幂等化（`_destroyed` 标记）+ 把上面每一条引用逐一斩断。

#### 4.5.2 核心流程

销毁链的执行顺序（顺序有意为之）：

```text
engine.destroy()                          # 用户显式调用
  └─ self._destroyed = True               # 先立标记（幂等 + __del__ 跳过依据）
  └─ destroy_exchanges(module)            # 只释放本引擎的 DeepEP 缓冲
  └─ 释放 DeepCompile 编译态 / dynamo 配置
  └─ optimizer.destroy()                  # 各优化器清理反向引用：
  │     ZeRO-3 (stage3):      parameter_offload.destroy()  → 摘模块 hook + 弹 FWD_MODULE_STACK（至多一次）
  │                            p._z3_optimizer = None、unpin 卸载缓冲
  │     ZeRO-1/2 (stage_1_and_2): p._hp_mapping = None、del p._zero_optimizer、unpin
  │     BF16:                  lp._hp_mapping = None、lp._hp_grad = None、摘 grad acc hooks
  └─ _deactivate_deepcompile()            # 若 DeepCompile 激活：先走它（会重新挂 forward hooks）
  └─ 摘除并置空三个引擎 hook:              # 必须在 _deactivate_deepcompile 之后！
        module_forward_pre_hook / module_forward_post_hook / first_dataloader_check
  └─ debug_clear_module_and_param_names()
  └─ decoupled checkpoint engine cleanup
  finally: 释放 python_gc 手持的代际

engine.__del__()                          # GC 兜底
  └─ if self._destroyed: return           # 已显式销毁 → 直接返回，防止二次拆除
  └─ 否则 try destroy()（异常仅 debug 日志）
```

**练习 2**：`p._hp_grad` 为什么危险系数特别高？测试里为什么用 storage 指针而不是 tensor 身份来判断？

**答案**：`_hp_grad` 是扁平 fp32 梯度缓冲的视图，体量约 2 倍 bf16 模型大小；视图对象本身很小，但它把整块缓冲的 **storage** 钉在内存里——即使缓冲的 tensor 对象已被 GC。所以测试比较 `untyped_storage().data_ptr()` 的集合交集（[test_zero.py:2334-2339](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/b9100c541ac1b8e25148bc8000d1ad45c4c095db/tests/unit/v1/zero/test_zero.py#L2334-L2339)），比 tensor 身份更能抓住这类泄漏。

**答案**：类级 `functools.lru_cache` 装饰方法时，缓存的 key 包含 `self`，且缓存永不失效——每个调用过的实例都永久留在缓存里，实例又引用模块与参数。改成每实例（`__init__` 里对绑定方法再包一层 `lru_cache`）后，缓存生命周期与实例绑定：实例可回收，缓存随之消失，缓存效果（按 `(submodule, step_id)` 记忆待释放参数集）不变。

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.
